items.behaviour_notes: The app does not change. Both generated targets stay byte-identical to their sources, and gen:shared rewrote nothing. scripts/gen-shared-mirror.mjs now reads scripts/shared-mirror.manifest.json (`--manifest <file>` points it at another one). Each entry has source, target, transform ("none" or "cjs-to-esm"), importRewrite, include/exclude, and keep (hand-written files in the target that are never written, never reported as extra and never removed). A source can be a directory or a single file. All entries are computed before any file is written, so a bad entry fails the whole run with nothing written. `--check` names the failing entry, for example "entry #2 (server/shared/expr/ -> mobile/src/shared/expr/vendor/)". The cjs-to-esm transform only rewrites the plain CommonJS patterns (require bindings, `module.exports = {...}`, a leading 'use strict') and refuses a file that still contains require/exports afterwards. The new second entry is mobile/src/shared/expr/vendor: it excludes corpus.mjs, sheet.mjs and sheetFill.mjs, which mobile never carried, and keeps index.d.mts. This makes it match exactly what exprVendor.lockstep.test.ts expects. Deviation from the item text: entries with transform "none" get no GENERATED header. The agent-hub sync test and the mobile lockstep test compare bytes, and the item requires the expr entry to stay byte-identical. The header is written only when a transform or importRewrite changes the text; this is documented in the script, the manifest $comment and CLAUDE.md. In CLAUDE.md the lint:shared-mirror bullet now names the mobile target and the manifest (a few lines, not the two sentences asked). The lockstep test comment now says to run npm run gen:shared.

Nothing in the app changed. Only the duplication gate changed.

1) .jscpd.json now ignores every generated file:
   - agent-hub/src/shared/** (this replaces the separate expr/** and webpage/** entries)
   - mobile/src/shared/expr/vendor/**
   - mobile/src/core/theme/generated/**
   - **/*.generated.js, **/*.generated.ts and **/*.generated.mjs (the last replaces agent-hub/src/**/*.generated.mjs)
   - server/core/markdown/editorSerialization.cjs and editorCollab.cjs
   - agent-hub/src/i18n/en-defaults.js
   - agent-hub/src/components/onboarding/generated/** and e2e/tests/generated/** (both carry a GENERATED header)
   - agent-hub/public/module-shims/**
   The ignore entries that were already there for bindings/mirror, components/*/ssrfGuard.js and htmlToMarkdown.js are kept.

   I used mobile/src/shared/expr/vendor/** instead of the item's mobile/src/shared/expr/**. Only vendor/ is generated: index.ts and the tests next to it are hand-written, so they still count.

2) scripts/duplication-ratchet.mjs now keeps two budgets, production and test.
   - A clone counts as test only when both of its ends are test files (exported isTestFile/groupOf). Any other clone counts as production, so the two numbers add up to jscpd's total.
   - jscpd 5's JSON report has no per-file statistics, so the split is computed from the clone list. If the clone lines do not add up to statistics.total.duplicatedLines, the script exits 2 rather than passing.
   - Each group is gated separately, and --update lowers each one on its own and never raises either.
   - --list shows the top 25 clones per group.
   - If the budget file lacks the two numbers (the old {duplicatedLines} format), the script measures and writes both, the same way a first run does.
   - The CLI code is wrapped in main(), so the test can import the classifier.

3) .jscpd-ratchet.json now holds production 15634 and test 26804, measured on the current tree. The old single budget was 49644; the current total is 42438.

4) The tests now also check that every target in scripts/shared-mirror.manifest.json matches an ignore glob in .jscpd.json, using path.matchesGlob. A new mirror entry without a jscpd ignore therefore fails test:scripts. They also check that hand-written neighbours (for example mobile/src/shared/expr/index.ts and registry.generated.test.ts) are not ignored.

The new server/utils/stableJson.js has two functions. The first is stableStringify(value, { undefined: 'null' | 'drop' | 'raw', toJSON }), which builds the text by hand with keys in Array#sort() order. The second is sortedKeysJson(value, { toJSON = true }), which runs JSON.stringify over a copy with keys sorted; the JS engine still puts integer-like keys first, in numeric order. I found 13 copies, not 9. Each caller keeps its function name, which is now a one-line wrapper, so call sites and exports are unchanged. Variant per caller:

- stableStringify with 'drop': templateUpgrade.

items.behaviour_notes: generic.py now imports is_valid_iban/luhn/ipv4/ipv6 from app.services.pii_validators under the old _-prefixed names, so registry.py and the pii_regex barrel are unchanged. The private copies are deleted, and so is the now-unused `import ipaddress`. _is_valid_iban_anysep stays and calls the shared IBAN check. The IPv6 copy was identical, so it is shared too. Only the IPv4 check behaves differently: the old copy accepted "+1.2.3.4" (int('+1')), and the shared one rejects it. Both accept " 1.2.3.4". In practice nothing changes for users, because _IPV4_RE (`\b(?:\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3}\b`) only ever produces digits and dots, so a sign or a space never reaches the validator. The new tests pin "+1.2.3.4" (rejected), " 1.2.3.4" (accepted), the bounds, IBAN/Luhn, anysep, and that generic's names are the same objects as pv's.
